q: I ___ a student.
She ___ two brothers.
___ you like pizza?
why: Fragen mit "you" im Present Simple bilden wir mit "Do".

q: There ___ a cat on the table.
This is ___ book.
why: Vor einem Nomen steht das Possessivpronomen "my".

q: What is the opposite of "big"?
I drink ___ in the morning.
My mother's sister is my ___.
It is 7 o'clock. Time to ___ up!

text: Hi, I'm Anna. I'm from Spain. I like music and swimming.
q: What does Anna like?
why: Im Text: "I like music and swimming."

text: The shop opens at 9 o'clock and closes at 6 o'clock.
q: When does the shop close?

text: Tom has a dog. The dog is brown. It likes to run in the park.
q: Where does the dog like to run?
I ___ to the cinema yesterday.
why: "yesterday" verlangt Simple Past; "go" ist unregelmäßig: went.

q: She is taller ___ her sister.
We ___ dinner when the phone rang.
why: Eine laufende Handlung, die unterbrochen wird: Past Continuous.

q: I have lived here ___ 2019.
You ___ park here. It's not allowed.
why: "mustn't" = nicht dürfen; "don't have to" = nicht müssen.

q: Can you ___ me your pen, please? I forgot mine.
My flight was ___ because of the storm, so I arrived late.
Please ___ the light when you leave the room.
He doesn't have a job. He is ___.

text: Sorry I'm late! My bus broke down, so I walked the last two miles. I'll be there in ten minutes.
q: Why is the writer late?

text: Dear Sam, thanks for the invitation. I'd love to come to your party on Saturday, but I have to work until 8. Can I arrive late?
q: What does the writer ask?
opts: If the party is on Sunday
If he can bring a friend

text: Max usually takes the train to work, but today he is driving because there is a strike.
q: Why is Max driving today?
If I ___ more time, I would learn Spanish.
why: Conditional II: if + Simple Past, would + Verb.

q: The house ___ in 1920.
why: Passiv im Simple Past: was/were + Partizip.

q: She asked me where ___.
why: In indirekten Fragen gilt die normale Satzstellung, ohne "do/did".

q: I'm not used to ___ up so early.
why: "be used to" wird von der -ing-Form gefolgt.

q: He said he ___ call me the next day.
why: In der indirekten Rede wird "will" zu "would".

q: The meeting was ___ until next week.
To ___ for the job, send your CV and a cover letter.
You can trust Jenny. She's very ___.
I can't ___ with this noise any longer!

text: Because of the heavy snow, all flights from Chicago were cancelled yesterday. Passengers can rebook for free.
q: What can passengers do?
opts: Get their money back in cash

text: I used to play football every weekend, but since I hurt my knee I mostly watch games on TV.
q: What does the writer do now?
why: "used to" = früher; jetzt schaut er meist im TV.

text: Although the restaurant was expensive, the food was disappointing and the service was slow. We won't go back.
q: What does the writer think?
By the time we arrived, the film ___.
why: Vorzeitigkeit in der Vergangenheit: Past Perfect.

q: I wish I ___ harder when I was at school.
why: Bedauern über die Vergangenheit: wish + Past Perfect.

q: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the documents.
why: Nach "Not only" am Satzanfang folgt Inversion mit do/did.

q: She suggested ___ a taxi because it was raining.
The report, ___ was published last week, caused a stir.
His excuse didn't sound very ___, so nobody believed him.
Sales have ___ by 15% compared to last year.
The two companies decided to ___ and form one bigger firm.
It's hard to ___ a living as a freelance artist.
why: Feste Wendung: "make a living" = seinen Lebensunterhalt verdienen.

text: Researchers found that people who take short walks after meals have lower blood sugar. However, the study was small, so more research is needed.
q: What can we conclude?
opts: Walking is proven to cure diabetes
The result is promising but not final
why: Kleine Studie, "more research is needed" = vielversprechend, aber nicht gesichert.

text: The CEO denied the rumours, insisting that the company had no plans to lay off staff. Yet several employees say they have already been told to look for other jobs.
q: What does the text suggest?
opts: The CEO's statement may not be true
why: "Yet" signalisiert den Widerspruch zur Aussage des CEO.

text: Rather than raising prices, the café cut its menu and reduced portion sizes, a move customers barely noticed.
q: What did the café do?
opts: Made portions smaller without raising prices

q: Had I known about the delay, I ___ earlier.
why: Invertierter Conditional III (Had I known = If I had known).

q: Hardly ___ the house when it started to pour.
why: Nach "Hardly" am Satzanfang: Inversion mit Past Perfect.

q: It is essential that every employee ___ the safety rules.
why: Subjunctive nach "essential that": Grundform ohne -s (BrE oft auch "should follow").

q: She behaved as though nothing ___ the day before.
why: Zeitlich vor der Vergangenheit: "as though" + Past Perfect.

q: I'd rather you ___ smoke in here.
why: "would rather" + Person + Simple Past, auch für die Gegenwart.

q: Don't take it seriously; he's just ___.
why: "pull someone's leg" = jemanden auf den Arm nehmen.

q: If you are "taken aback", you are ___.
The plan sounds good, but his story just doesn't hold ___.
why: Idiom: "doesn't hold water" = hält einer Prüfung nicht stand.

q: The mayor's decision caused a public ___, and thousands signed a petition.

text: The film's visuals are undeniably stunning, yet one cannot help feeling that style has been prioritised at the expense of substance.
q: What is the writer's view?
opts: Beautiful to look at but lacking depth
Strong in both look and story
why: "style at the expense of substance" = Optik auf Kosten des Inhalts.

text: Far from being a setback, the failed launch proved a blessing in disguise: it exposed flaws that would have been far costlier to fix later.
q: How does the writer see the failed launch?

text: While few would dispute that remote work offers flexibility, critics argue that it quietly erodes the informal exchanges from which new ideas often spring.
q: What is the critics' main concern?
opts: Loss of spontaneous contact that sparks ideas
why: "erodes the informal exchanges" = spontaner Austausch geht verloren.
